indications.description: Aggressive and symptomatic medullary thyroid cancer with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic disease.

treatment.schedule_summary: Vandetanib 300 mg once daily, continuously, until progression or unacceptable side effects.
treatment.duration_text: Continuous until progression or unacceptable toxicity

action.message: Do not start vandetanib when baseline QTc is greater than 480 ms.

action.message: A single QTc ≥500 ms requires stopping vandetanib. Correct electrolytes; restart only after specialist confirmation and dose reduction.

action.message: Establish baseline versus on-treatment phase: initiation threshold >480 ms differs from the on-treatment ≥500 ms stop threshold.

action.message: Vandetanib is not recommended in moderate/severe renal impairment. The NCCP table does not assign numeric CrCl bands; do not infer one.

action.message: Not recommended with serum bilirubin >1.5 × ULN because safety and efficacy are not established.

rules.explanation: Not recommended with serum bilirubin >1.5 × ULN because safety and efficacy are not established.

action.message: Temporarily stop. Once resolved or improved to grade 1, consultant confirms reduced dose: first occurrence 200 mg/day; second 100 mg/day. Adverse reactions may persist because of the long half-life.

rules.explanation: Temporarily stop. Once resolved or improved to grade 1, consultant confirms reduced dose: first occurrence 200 mg/day; second 100 mg/day. Adverse reactions may persist because of the long half-life.

action.message: Retain toxicity history after apparent recovery: first grade ≥3 episode leads to 200 mg/day, second to 100 mg/day after recovery to ≤grade 1; further episodes require individual review.

rules.explanation: Retain toxicity history after apparent recovery: first grade ≥3 episode leads to 200 mg/day, second to 100 mg/day after recovery to ≤grade 1; further episodes require individual review.

action.message: No automatic restart. Table 2 states QTc <450 ms or confirmed pretreatment QTc with electrolyte correction; paragraph on p4 requires return to pretreatment status. Reconcile these source statements and current SmPC with cardiology/oncology; resume only at a reduced dose if authorised.
